name: Studded Lizard
body:
Studded Lizard CR 5

A blue-black, forked tongue flicks out of this stocky lizard’s mouth as it sniffs out its next meal.

XP 1,600
N Small animal
Init +6; Senses low-light vision, scent, tremorsense 60 ft.; Perception +16

DEFENSE

AC 19, touch 13, flat-footed 17 (+2 Dex, +6 natural, +1 size)
hp 52 (7d8+21)
Fort +8, Ref +4, Will +8
Defensive Abilities Dr 5/bludgeoning or piercing

OFFENSE

Speed 20 ft.
Melee bite +10 (1d6+7 plus 5 bleed [anticoagulant saliva] plus poison)
Space 5 ft.; Reach 5 ft.

STATISTICS

Str 20, Dex 14, Con 17, Int 2, Wis 16, Cha 6
Base Atk +5; CMB +9 (includes -1 size modifier); CMD 21 (includes -1 size modifier)
Feats Improved Initiative, Improved Natural Armor, Skill Focus (Perception), Skill Focus (Stealth)
Skills Climb +14, Perception +16, Stealth +19, Swim +9; Size Modifier +4 Stealth
Languages —
Sq anticoagulant saliva, mimic, slowing venom

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Anticoagulant Saliva (Ex)

When a studded lizard makes a successful bite attack against a creature, the creature takes 5 points of bleed damage.

Mimic (Ex)

A studded lizard changes the pigmentation and patterns on its skin to exactly mimic other non-venomous lizards native to the desert. The DC to identify the studded lizard is 5 higher than normal to see past this ruse and correctly identify it. On a failed skill check, the studded lizard is incorrectly identified as a native, nonthreatening lizard that feeds on insects.

Poison (Ex)

Bite—injury; save Fort DC 15; onset immediate; frequency 1 round; effect 1d4 Constitution damage and 1d2 Dexterity damage. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Slowing Venom (Ex)

A creature’s speed is decreased by 5 feet for every point of Dexterity damage that it takes from the studded lizard’s poison. Slowing Venom can’t reduce a creature’s speed to less than 5 feet. A creature’s speed is restored if the poison is neutralized or when the Dexterity damage is healed, whichever comes first.

ECOLOGY

Environment desert
Organization solitary
Treasure none

Lost Atlanteans, Copyright 2024, Bloodstone Press; author Beth Jones
